title: Joshua Chapter 2 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Joshua chapter 2 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Joshua Chapter 2 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Joshua Chapter 2.

questions.question: Who did Joshua send to spy secretly out of Shittim?
options: Two men
Three men
A woman
A group of elders
questions.correctAnswer: Two men
questions.explanation: Joshua 2:1 states that Joshua sent out two men to spy secretly.

questions.question: Where did the two men go to lodge when they entered Jericho?
options: A harlot's house
The king's palace
A temple
A farmer's field
questions.correctAnswer: A harlot's house
questions.explanation: Joshua 2:1 says the two men came into a harlot's house named Rahab and lodged there.

questions.question: True or False: The king of Jericho was informed that men from Israel came to search the country at night.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 2:2 reports that it was told to the king of Jericho that men of Israel came in at night to search the country.

questions.question: What did the king of Jericho command Rahab to do?
options: Bring forth the men lodged in her house
Hide the men
Kill the men
Send a message to Joshua
questions.correctAnswer: Bring forth the men lodged in her house
questions.explanation: Joshua 2:3 says the king sent to Rahab commanding her to bring forth the men who had come into her house.

questions.question: How did Rahab respond when the king's men asked for the spies?
options: She hid them and said she did not know where they were
She told the king where they were
She sent them away immediately
She captured them
questions.correctAnswer: She hid them and said she did not know where they were
questions.explanation: Joshua 2:4 explains that Rahab took the men, hid them, and told the king's men that she did not know where they were.

questions.question: True or False: Rahab hid the two men under flax on the roof of her house.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 2:6 states that Rahab hid the men on the roof with stalks of flax she had laid in order.

questions.question: When did the two men leave Rahab's house?
options: At the time of shutting the gate when it was dark
At dawn
At noon
At midnight
questions.correctAnswer: At the time of shutting the gate when it was dark
questions.explanation: Joshua 2:5 records that about the time of shutting the gate, when it was dark, the men went out.

questions.question: Who pursued the two men after they left Rahab's house?
options: The king's men
Rahab
Joshua's army
No one pursued them
questions.correctAnswer: The king's men
questions.explanation: Joshua 2:7 states that the men pursued the two spies the way to Jordan to the fords.

questions.question: True or False: After the pursuers left Jericho, the city gate was shut.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 2:7 mentions that as soon as the pursuers were gone out, they shut the gate.

questions.question: What did Rahab do before the men laid down to rest?
options: She came up to them on the roof
She left the city
She told the king about them
She gave them food and drink
questions.correctAnswer: She came up to them on the roof
questions.explanation: Joshua 2:8 says that before they laid down, Rahab came up to them upon the roof.

questions.question: In Joshua 2, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
options: Hide the men with stalks of flax on the roof
Swear kindness to Rahab's family
Send men to spy out Jericho
Tie a scarlet thread in the window
questions.correctAnswer: Send men to spy out Jericho
questions.explanation: Joshua 2:1 shows that Joshua first sent men to spy out Jericho before any other instructions or actions occurred.

questions.question: True or False: Rahab declared she did not know where the men came from when asked by the king's men.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 2:4 records Rahab saying she did not know whence the men were when questioned.

questions.question: What was Rahab's house's location relative to the city wall?
options: Upon the town wall
In the city center
Outside the city gates
On a hill outside Jericho
questions.correctAnswer: Upon the town wall
questions.explanation: Joshua 2:15 states that Rahab's house was upon the town wall and she dwelt upon the wall.

questions.question: What did Rahab use to lower the two men from her house?
options: A cord
A ladder
A basket
A rope made of flax
questions.correctAnswer: A cord
questions.explanation: Joshua 2:15 says she let them down by a cord through the window.

questions.question: What did the men instruct Rahab to do with the pursuers after they left?
options: Hide on the mountain for three days
Go to the king's palace
Hide in a cave
Escape to another city
questions.correctAnswer: Hide on the mountain for three days
questions.explanation: Joshua 2:16 advises Rahab to go to the mountain and hide there three days until the pursuers return.

medium.title: Joshua Chapter 2 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Joshua Chapter 2 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What reason does Rahab give for her confidence that the LORD has given the land to the Israelites?
options: Because the LORD dried up the Red Sea for them
Because their terror has fallen upon us and all inhabitants faint because of them
Because they destroyed the two kings of the Amorites
Because Joshua is a great leader
questions.correctAnswer: Because their terror has fallen upon us and all inhabitants faint because of them
questions.explanation: Rahab states her confidence in Joshua 2:9 that 'the LORD hath given you the land, and that your terror is fallen upon us, and that all the inhabitants of the land faint because of you.' This shows the fear and recognition of God's power among the people.

questions.question: According to Joshua 2:10, which past event caused the inhabitants to fear the Israelites?
options: The parting of the Red Sea
The destruction of Jericho
The crossing of the Jordan River
The defeat of Sihon and Og
questions.correctAnswer: The defeat of Sihon and Og
questions.explanation: Verse 10 explains that the fear came from hearing how God dried up the Red Sea and what was done to the two kings of the Amorites, Sihon and Og, showing God's power in past victories.

questions.question: What effect did hearing of Israel’s deeds have on the hearts of the inhabitants, according to Joshua 2:11?
options: They became angry and planned a rebellion
Their hearts melted and courage failed
They sought peace with Israel
They ignored the news
questions.correctAnswer: Their hearts melted and courage failed
questions.explanation: Joshua 2:11 states that on hearing these things, 'our hearts did melt, neither did there remain any more courage in any man,' showing complete loss of bravery due to fear of Israel’s God.

questions.question: How does Rahab demonstrate faith and trust in God in her interaction with the spies?
options: By hiding the spies and asking for a promise of protection
By telling the king where the spies were
By refusing to help the spies
By joining the Israelites directly
questions.correctAnswer: By hiding the spies and asking for a promise of protection
questions.explanation: Rahab hides the spies (2:4, 2:6) and then requests they swear kindness to her family (2:12-13), showing her trust in God's power and seeking mercy based on that faith.

questions.question: What specific request does Rahab make to the spies regarding her family?
options: That they protect and save her father, mother, brothers, and sisters
That they give her land in Israel
That they teach her about the LORD
That they take her family to Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: That they protect and save her father, mother, brothers, and sisters
questions.explanation: In Joshua 2:13, Rahab asks them to save alive her entire family and deliver their lives from death, showing her concern for their safety tied to her kindness to the spies.

questions.question: What promise do the spies give Rahab in response to her request for protection?
options: They will kill anyone who harms her family
They will deal kindly and truly with her when the LORD gives them the land
They will make her a leader in Israel
They will send her family to another land
questions.correctAnswer: They will deal kindly and truly with her when the LORD gives them the land
questions.explanation: Joshua 2:14 states the spies' promise: 'Our life for yours... we will deal kindly and truly with thee' upon the LORD giving them the land, affirming integrity and faithfulness.

questions.question: How does Rahab help the spies escape from Jericho?
options: She disguises them as merchants
She lets them down by a cord through a window in the city wall
She hides them in a cave outside the city
She bribes the king's guards
questions.correctAnswer: She lets them down by a cord through a window in the city wall
questions.explanation: Joshua 2:15 describes Rahab lowering the spies by a cord through her window because her house was upon the town wall, facilitating their escape.

questions.question: What instructions does Rahab give the spies for their safety after escaping?
options: Go to the mountain and hide for three days until the pursuers return
Return immediately to Joshua
Hide inside her house until the attack
Cross the Jordan River at once
questions.correctAnswer: Go to the mountain and hide for three days until the pursuers return
questions.explanation: Joshua 2:16 records Rahab telling them to hide in the mountain for three days until their pursuers return, ensuring their safety before continuing their journey.

questions.question: According to Joshua 2:18, what is the purpose of the scarlet thread Rahab must bind in her window?
options: To signal the Israelites where to attack
To mark her house so her family will be spared
To warn the king of Jericho
To decorate her house for the festival
questions.correctAnswer: To mark her house so her family will be spared
questions.explanation: Verse 18 explains the scarlet thread in the window serves as a sign so that Rahab's household will be spared when the Israelites take the land, symbolizing protection through obedience.

questions.question: What consequence is given in Joshua 2:19 for anyone who leaves Rahab’s house during the attack?
options: They will be protected by the Israelites
Their blood shall be upon their own head
They will receive a reward
They will be made prisoners
questions.correctAnswer: Their blood shall be upon their own head
questions.explanation: Joshua 2:19 clearly states that anyone who goes out of the house into the street will be responsible for their own blood, enforcing the importance of staying within the marked house for safety.

questions.question: What condition would nullify the oath the spies made to Rahab, according to Joshua 2:20?
options: If she hides the spies again
If she tells anyone about their mission
If she leaves Jericho before the attack
If she removes the scarlet thread
questions.correctAnswer: If she tells anyone about their mission
questions.explanation: Verse 20 states that if Rahab reveals the spies’ business, then the spies will be free from the oath, emphasizing the importance of secrecy and trust.

questions.question: How does Joshua 2:22 demonstrate the faithfulness of the spies to Rahab’s safety?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 2:22 shows the spies hid on the mountain for three days and were not found by the pursuers, demonstrating their obedience to Rahab’s instructions and their commitment to keeping the promise made to her.

questions.question: Based on Joshua 2:23-24, what is the spies’ report to Joshua about the land and its inhabitants?
options: The land is fortified and the inhabitants are strong
The LORD has delivered the land into their hands and all inhabitants faint because of Israel
The inhabitants are prepared to fight to the death
The land is barren and uninhabited
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD has delivered the land into their hands and all inhabitants faint because of Israel
questions.explanation: Verses 23-24 confirm the spies reported that God has delivered the land and the inhabitants are fearful and discouraged, reinforcing the theme of God’s sovereign power and Israel’s confidence.

questions.question: How does Joshua 2:12-16 illustrate the biblical virtue of integrity in Rahab's actions and requests?
options: Rahab deceives the king but honestly asks for a promise of protection
Rahab hides the spies and asks for a truthful oath concerning her family's safety
Rahab betrays the spies for personal gain
Rahab refuses to act out of fear
questions.correctAnswer: Rahab hides the spies and asks for a truthful oath concerning her family's safety
questions.explanation: These verses show Rahab’s integrity by risking her life to protect the spies and requesting a solemn oath (2:12-13, 2:17-21) that the Israelites will protect her family, highlighting trust and honesty.

questions.question: True or False: According to Joshua 2:14, the spies’ promise to Rahab is conditional on her keeping their mission secret.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 2:14 says 'Our life for yours, if ye utter not this our business,' indicating their promise depends on Rahab's discretion and secrecy.

hard.title: Joshua Chapter 2 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Joshua Chapter 2.

questions.question: What condition did the spies set for Rahab to ensure her family's safety?
options: She must hide the spies forever.
She must bind a scarlet thread in her window.
She must flee to the mountains with her family.
She must pay a ransom to the king of Jericho.
questions.correctAnswer: She must bind a scarlet thread in her window.
questions.explanation: Joshua 2:18 states that Rahab must bind a scarlet thread in the window to mark her house for protection when the Israelites come into the land.

questions.question: What did the spies promise would happen if Rahab revealed their mission?
options: They would return and punish her family.
They would break the oath made to her.
They would never enter Jericho.
They would make her a queen.
questions.correctAnswer: They would break the oath made to her.
questions.explanation: Joshua 2:20 says that if Rahab reveals the spies' mission, the spies would be released from the oath they made to her, implying she would no longer be protected.

questions.question: How long did the spies stay hidden on the mountain after leaving Rahab's house?
options: One day
Two days
Three days
Seven days
questions.correctAnswer: Three days
questions.explanation: Joshua 2:22 states the spies stayed on the mountain for three days until the pursuers returned and could not find them.

questions.question: What was the spies' assessment of the inhabitants of the land after their mission?
options: They were strong and fearless.
They were united against the Israelites.
They had fainted and lost courage because of the Israelites.
They were unaware of the Israelites' approach.
questions.correctAnswer: They had fainted and lost courage because of the Israelites.
questions.explanation: Joshua 2:24 reports the spies told Joshua that the inhabitants of the land faint because of the Israelites, showing fear and weakness.

questions.question: What literary device is demonstrated by the scarlet thread in Rahab's window symbolizing both protection and salvation?
options: Foreshadowing
Chiasm
Inclusio
Metonymy
questions.correctAnswer: Foreshadowing
questions.explanation: The scarlet thread (Joshua 2:18, 21) foreshadows later biblical themes of salvation and protection, such as the blood of the Passover lamb in Exodus 12.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage closely connects with Rahab's scarlet cord as a symbol of protection?
options: Exodus 12:13 - The blood on the doorposts during Passover
Genesis 12:3 - The promise to Abraham
Leviticus 16:30 - The Day of Atonement rituals
Deuteronomy 6:4 - The Shema declaration
questions.correctAnswer: Exodus 12:13 - The blood on the doorposts during Passover
questions.explanation: The scarlet cord in Joshua 2:18 echoes the Passover blood on doorposts in Exodus 12:13, both serving as markers of divine protection from judgment.

questions.question: What was the spies' oath to Rahab regarding her and her household?
options: They would enslave her family.
They would protect and save her family alive.
They would exile her family.
They would make her family priests.
questions.correctAnswer: They would protect and save her family alive.
questions.explanation: Joshua 2:14 states the men promised to save Rahab and her family alive if she kept their mission secret.

questions.question: What did Rahab use to hide the spies on her roof?
options: Baskets of figs
Stacks of flax stalks
Bundles of wheat
Piles of stones
questions.correctAnswer: Stacks of flax stalks
questions.explanation: Joshua 2:6 explains that Rahab hid the spies under stalks of flax she had laid out on the roof.

questions.question: True or False: The spies instructed Rahab to have her entire household remain inside the house once the Israelites attacked Jericho.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 2:19 states that anyone who leaves Rahab's house will bear their own blood, implying the household must stay inside for protection.

questions.question: True or False: Joshua's spies were caught by the pursuers after leaving Rahab's house.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joshua 2:22 says the pursuers sought the spies but found them not, indicating the spies successfully evaded capture.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage references Rahab's faith and actions as an example of faith in action?
options: Hebrews 11:31
Romans 5:1
James 2:25
Both Hebrews 11:31 and James 2:25
questions.correctAnswer: Both Hebrews 11:31 and James 2:25
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:31 and James 2:25 both commend Rahab for her faith and hospitality, linking her story in Joshua 2 to New Testament teachings on faith.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word for 'scarlet' (שָׁנִי, shani) often symbolize in biblical literature, as seen in this chapter?
options: Sin and judgment
Royalty and kingship
Purification and protection
Death and mourning
questions.correctAnswer: Purification and protection
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'shani' for scarlet, as in Joshua 2:18, is often associated with purification and protection, similar to its use in the red thread in the red heifer ritual (Numbers 19).

questions.question: What was the historical-cultural significance of Rahab's house being on the city wall?
options: It was common for harlots to live on city walls as watchmen.
It facilitated communication with the outside and escape, as in Rahab letting the spies down by a cord.
It was a place for royal officials to reside.
It was a marketplace for trading goods.
questions.correctAnswer: It facilitated communication with the outside and escape, as in Rahab letting the spies down by a cord.
questions.explanation: Joshua 2:15 shows Rahab's house was on the wall which allowed her to lower the spies down by a cord, a strategic location for espionage and escape in ancient Near Eastern cities.

questions.question: What is the theological significance of Rahab's recognition of the LORD as 'God in heaven above, and in earth beneath' in this chapter?
options: It shows her exclusive worship of Canaanite gods.
It reflects the universal sovereignty of Yahweh acknowledged even by Gentiles.
It indicates her rejection of all gods.
It is a direct quote from the Ten Commandments.
questions.correctAnswer: It reflects the universal sovereignty of Yahweh acknowledged even by Gentiles.
questions.explanation: Joshua 2:11 reveals Rahab's acknowledgment of Yahweh's universal power, a theme that shows God's dominion beyond Israel and foreshadows the inclusion of Gentiles in God's plan.

questions.question: How does the story of Rahab and the spies serve as a typology for New Testament themes?
options: It foreshadows Jesus' betrayal by Judas.
It exemplifies faith leading to salvation and inclusion in God's covenant community.
It represents the final judgment against sinners.
It illustrates the need for strict legalism.
questions.correctAnswer: It exemplifies faith leading to salvation and inclusion in God's covenant community.
questions.explanation: Rahab's faith and protection by the scarlet cord (Joshua 2:18) foreshadow New Testament themes of faith's role in salvation and Gentile inclusion, as seen in Hebrews 11 and James 2.

theological.title: Joshua Chapter 2 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Joshua Chapter 2 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Rahab's recognition in Joshua 2:9-11 primarily reveal about God's nature?
options: God is unknowable and distant
God is sovereign and instills fear in nations
God is indifferent to earthly kingdoms
God only acts through natural events
questions.correctAnswer: God is sovereign and instills fear in nations
questions.explanation: Joshua 2:9-11 shows Rahab acknowledging that the LORD has given the land to Israel and that their terror has fallen upon the inhabitants, revealing God's sovereignty over nations and His power to instill fear as a judgment.

questions.question: Which doctrine is illustrated by Rahab's plea for protection of her family in Joshua 2:12-13?
options: The doctrine of sanctification
The doctrine of covenant faithfulness and mercy
The doctrine of predestination
The doctrine of divine retribution
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of covenant faithfulness and mercy
questions.explanation: In Joshua 2:12-13, Rahab asks for kindness in return for her kindness, illustrating the biblical doctrine that God’s people extend mercy and covenant faithfulness, reflecting God’s merciful character.

questions.question: How do Joshua 2:1 and 2:15 together typologically foreshadow Christ's redemptive work?
options: Christ is portrayed as a judge of sinners
Christ provides a means of salvation through a 'cord' or 'rope' of deliverance
Christ is depicted as a military leader only
Christ is shown as a lawgiver
questions.correctAnswer: Christ provides a means of salvation through a 'cord' or 'rope' of deliverance
questions.explanation: Joshua 2:1 introduces the spies lodging in Rahab’s house, and 2:15 speaks of Rahab letting them down by a cord through the window. This cord symbolizes salvation, prefiguring Christ as the means of deliverance from judgment.

questions.question: What attribute of God is especially emphasized in Joshua 2:10 concerning the Red Sea and the Amorite kings?
options: God's patience
God's omnipresence
God's power and faithfulness to His promises
God's mercy alone without judgment
questions.correctAnswer: God's power and faithfulness to His promises
questions.explanation: Joshua 2:10 recounts how God dried up the Red Sea and destroyed the Amorite kings, demonstrating His mighty power and faithfulness to deliver His people as He promised.

questions.question: Considering Joshua 2:16-17 and 2:20-21, what theological principle is taught about oaths and covenant obligations?
options: Oaths are optional and can be broken without consequence
God’s people are bound to uphold oaths made in His name
Oaths made to enemies are not binding
Oaths are only symbolic and have no real meaning
questions.correctAnswer: God’s people are bound to uphold oaths made in His name
questions.explanation: Joshua 2:16-17 and 2:20-21 reveal that the spies take Rahab’s oath seriously and promise to keep it, teaching that oaths sworn by the LORD must be honored as part of covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: How does Joshua 2:22-24 demonstrate God’s providential protection over His plans?
options: God abandoned the spies to their fate
The spies were hidden and safely returned, showing God's providential care
The spies failed and were captured
God intervened only through natural means
questions.correctAnswer: The spies were hidden and safely returned, showing God's providential care
questions.explanation: Joshua 2:22-24 narrates how the spies were hidden and escaped pursuit, illustrating God’s providential protection ensuring His plans for Israel’s conquest succeeded.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching emerges from Joshua 2:4 and 2:14 concerning human agency and divine sovereignty?
options: Human actions are irrelevant to divine plans
Human decisions cooperate with God’s sovereign will
Only divine action matters, human effort is futile
Human agency overrides divine sovereignty
questions.correctAnswer: Human decisions cooperate with God’s sovereign will
questions.explanation: Joshua 2:4 shows Rahab hiding the spies by her own decision, and 2:14 shows the men promising protection in return. This reveals that human choices participate in God’s sovereign plan of salvation.

questions.question: What narrative arc is deepened by Joshua 2:23-24 about Israel’s conquest of Canaan?
options: Israel’s conquest is purely military without divine involvement
Israel’s conquest is assured by divine deliverance and the fear of their enemies
The conquest is uncertain and fraught with human failure
The conquest is delayed indefinitely
questions.correctAnswer: Israel’s conquest is assured by divine deliverance and the fear of their enemies
questions.explanation: Joshua 2:23-24 shows the spies reporting God's hand delivering the land and the inhabitants’ fear, emphasizing the biblical theme that conquest is enabled by God’s power and judgment.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Joshua 2 promotes deception by Rahab. What does Joshua 2:4-6 and 2:14-17 actually teach about righteousness and divine justice?
options: Deception is always condemned without exception
Divine justice accommodates wise and faithful acts to preserve life
Rahab’s actions were sinful with no justification
God endorses all human actions
questions.correctAnswer: Divine justice accommodates wise and faithful acts to preserve life
questions.explanation: Joshua 2:4-6 and 2:14-17 show Rahab’s hiding of the spies and covenant to protect life, teaching that God’s justice values faithfulness and preservation of life, even if it involves cunning, within His sovereign plan.

questions.question: What does Joshua 2:18-19 teach about the doctrine of covenant protection and its conditions?
options: Protection is unconditional regardless of behavior
Covenant protection requires obedience and trust in God’s appointed sign
Protection is based on human merit alone
The covenant sign is irrelevant for safety
questions.correctAnswer: Covenant protection requires obedience and trust in God’s appointed sign
questions.explanation: Joshua 2:18-19 instructs Rahab to bind the scarlet thread as a sign for protection and warns that anyone leaving the house forfeits this protection, showing covenantal conditionality on obedience and faith.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is highlighted by Joshua 2:11 when Rahab states, 'for the LORD your God, he is God in heaven above, and in earth beneath'?
options: God’s omnipotence and universal sovereignty
God’s limited jurisdiction
God’s silence in worldly affairs
God’s partiality to nations
questions.correctAnswer: God’s omnipotence and universal sovereignty
questions.explanation: Joshua 2:11 affirms God’s universal reign over heaven and earth, emphasizing His omnipotence and sovereignty over all creation.

questions.question: What synthesis of verses 2:7 and 2:22 teaches about God’s providential timing in protecting His people?
options: God’s protection is random and unplanned
God orchestrates events so enemies fail to capture His people
God’s protection depends solely on human strength
God intervenes only after failure
questions.correctAnswer: God orchestrates events so enemies fail to capture His people
questions.explanation: Joshua 2:7 shows the pursuers chasing the spies until they crossed Jordan, and 2:22 shows the spies hiding until the pursuers returned and failed to find them, illustrating divine providence preventing capture.

questions.question: How does Joshua 2:1-2 reveal the human and divine roles in the unfolding of Israel’s conquest plan?
options: Only human initiative is involved
Only God acts without human participation
Human reconnaissance runs parallel to divine sovereignty
The event is purely accidental
questions.correctAnswer: Human reconnaissance runs parallel to divine sovereignty
questions.explanation: Joshua 2:1-2 recounts Joshua sending spies, showing human responsibility, while the overall success depends on God’s sovereign hand, combining human action with divine providence.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning fear and faith is taught by the inhabitants’ reaction in Joshua 2:11 and 2:24?
options: Fear of God leads to despair and hopelessness
Fear of the LORD’s power leads to fainting and acknowledgment of His sovereignty
Fear is unrelated to faith
Fear is always sinful
questions.correctAnswer: Fear of the LORD’s power leads to fainting and acknowledgment of His sovereignty
questions.explanation: Joshua 2:11 and 2:24 describe the inhabitants fainting in fear of Israel, showing that fear of God’s power leads to recognition of His sovereign authority, a biblical response to divine judgment.

questions.question: What theological insight about salvation and human response arises from Rahab’s actions and the spies’ promise in Joshua 2:12-14?
options: Salvation is automatic without human involvement
Salvation involves human faith and God’s promise of protection
Salvation depends on human works alone
Salvation is only national, not individual
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation involves human faith and God’s promise of protection
questions.explanation: Joshua 2:12-14 shows Rahab’s faith in asking for protection and the spies’ promise to save her family, demonstrating the biblical principle that salvation requires human faith combined with God’s gracious promise.
